land.text: the land called Tang, which King Cheng of Zhou gave to his younger brother Tang Shuyu; the page does not locate Tang

predecessors.note: A Zhou fief ('King Cheng of Zhou... gave the land called Tang'); the 1042 BC year is the rulers table's. The core radius is the researcher's reading (confidence 1 on the place).

land.text: Han, one of the three states that divided Jin's lands in 403 BC

successors.note: 403: 'they divided the state's lands among themselves'; Han and Zhao took the last Jin land (Partition of Jin gives 349; Warring States period gives 376; the Jin page gives 369 as the last year).

land.text: Wei, one of the three states that divided Jin's lands in 403 BC
Zhao, one of the three states that divided Jin's lands in 403 BC

capitals.name: Tang, then E, then Jiang (the page lists the capitals in this order without years)
capitals.note: Years: the page gives no dates for Tang, E or Jiang ('The capital was later moved to E, then Jiang, then Xintian'); the span end is the researcher's boundary (page silent, confidence 1). Quwo, 'the capital of a fragment of Jin' 746-677, is a rival seat, not drawn.

capitals.name: Xintian (Houma)
capitals.note: The move to Xintian is undated on the page (page silent); 585 is the researcher's boundary. After 403 the dukes kept only the area around Jiang and Quwo.

rulers.name: Marquis Jing of Jin
rulers.note: Earlier marquises (Shu Yu of Tang 1042 BC, Xie, Wu, Cheng, Li d. 859) have no reign years on the page and are omitted. The rival Quwo line (Huan Shu 745-732, Zhuang Bo 731-716, Duke Wu of Quwo 715-679) is not listed.

rulers.name: Duke Wu of Jin (of Quwo)
rulers.title: Duke
rulers.note: Duke of Quwo from 715; 'Duke of Jin' 678-677 after conquering Jin.

rulers.name: Duke Jing (or Ai, or Yi) of Jin
Duke Huan (or Xiao) of Jin
rulers.note: Last Jin ruler; the Bamboo Annals 'moved Duke Huan to Tunliu, and after that there were no more records'.

correction.text: Tang, the land King Cheng of Zhou gave to Tang Shuyu; the page does not locate it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the fief before Cliopatria's first shape (-750): Tang, 'the land called Tang' given to Tang Shuyu (rulers table '1042 BC'). The page does not locate Tang or give any area, so the 70 km radius around Linfen (about 15,000 km2) is the researcher's reading, confidence 1 on the place; a vassal tint of the Zhou until 751 (the zhou-dynasty dossier).

136,796 km2 for 750-551. Unverified: page budget. The page implies a far smaller Jin for most of this span: a divided state from 746 ('From 746 to 677 BC, Quwo was the capital of a fragment of Jin'), reunited only when 'In 678 BC, Duke Wu of Quwo conquered Jin', then growing when Duke Xian (676-651) 'annexed 16 or 17 small states in Shanxi' and 'absorbed a number of Rong tribes'. No page opened gives an extent, so the shape stands and the ledger carries the dated steps; a gap-filler should open 'Spring and Autumn period' and the Jin annexation pages. The page has no area figure.

152,647 km2 for 550-451. Cliopatria moves 84 cells of the Hebei plain (115.5-116.9 E, 36.0-38.3 N) from Qi to Jin in 550; no page opened dates or names that land (confidence 1 in the ledger). Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Jin as drawn, without the Zhou royal seat at Luoyang

keyframe_review.note: 152,603 km2 for 450-405. Drawn whole until 405 as Cliopatria does, although the real power had passed: 'Zhao, Han, and Wei clans annihilated the Zhi clan' in 453, the Zhi having been the dominant clan, and the dukes were left 'only Jiang County and Quwo County' (Duke You, 433-416). The shape is kept so that the land has an owner until the three states' own shapes begin in 404; the rump that outlived the partition is the next keyframe. One correction: Cliopatria's 450 shape takes the Luoyang strip (15 cells, 112.2-113.2 E, 34.6-34.9 N) from the Zhou royal domain, but the court sat at Chengzhou near Luoyang until 256 (Eastern Zhou page), so the Luoyang disc is removed (see the eastern-zhou dossier); the Henei side that Jin really received in 635 is a ledger gain. Cliopatria also moves a strip on the Henei/Wey side (9 cells) into Jin and 21 cells at the Luhun edge (110.7-112.1 E, 34.3-34.6 N) to Chu; no page opened dates either.

correction.text: Jiang County and Quwo County, the area around Jiang and Quwo left to the dukes

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -404..-370: Cliopatria's Jin row ends in 405 and Han, Wei and Zhao begin in 404, but the Jin line went on: 'leaving only Jiang County and Quwo County (both in modern-day Shanxi Province) for Duke You of Jin' (403-paragraph), the last duke, Huan, reigning to 369. Radius 45 km around Houma (Xintian) covers both counties, the researcher's reading. The three pages disagree on the end: 386/376 deposition of Duke Jing, 349 Han and Zhao dividing the rest (Partition of Jin), 376 'marking the end of the Jin state' (Warring States period), 369 (Jin page).

ledger.note: c. 1042: King Cheng gives Tang to his brother, founding Jin. 'King Cheng of Zhou... gave the land called Tang (唐)... to his younger brother, Tang Shuyu'; rulers table 'Shu Yu of Tang 1042 BC–?'; infobox 'Established: 11th century BC'. Tang's place and size are not on the page.

region.text: Quwo, 'the capital of a fragment of Jin'

ledger.note: 746: a branch holds Quwo against the Jin marquises. 'From 746 to 677 BC, Quwo (曲沃) was the capital of a fragment of Jin'; the rulers table starts the Quwo line (Huan Shu) in 745. The page does not give a front line, so the zone is the Quwo area.
678: Duke Wu of Quwo conquers Jin. 'In 678 BC, Duke Wu of Quwo conquered Jin and killed Marquis Min of Jin (704–678).'
678: the Quwo branch takes the Jin throne. The rulers table passes from Marquis Min to 'Duke Wu of Quwo and Jin' (678-677 as Duke of Jin); same state, same colour.

ledger.counterpart: small states of Shanxi (Geng, Huo, old Wei, Yu, Western Guo)
ledger.note: 676-651: Duke Xian annexes the small states of Shanxi. 'He annexed 16 or 17 small states in Shanxi, dominated 38 others, and absorbed a number of Rong tribes'; 'Some of the states conquered were Geng (耿), Huo (霍), old Wei (魏), Yu (虞) and Western Guo.' The page dates only the reign (676-651), not the conquests, and does not locate the states; the region is the Shanxi part of Cliopatria's 750 shape, a reading.

635: King Xiang rewards Duke Wen of Jin with Henei and Yangfan. Eastern Zhou page, Chaos of Prince Dai paragraph (635): Duke Wen 'killed Prince Dai and was rewarded with rule over Henei and Yangfan'. The sentence has no year of its own; the place of Yangfan (Jiyuan) is the researcher's. Cliopatria never draws this land in Jin.

region.text: the Hebei-plain strip (115.5-116.9 E, 36.0-38.3 N) that Cliopatria moves from Qi to Jin

ledger.note: 550: Cliopatria's Jin shape grows by about 17,000 km2 at Qi's expense. Page silent: nothing on the Jin page or the Partition of Jin page dates or names this land; the year is the shape's. Unverified: page budget.
450: 9 cells of Wey's shape pass to Jin in Cliopatria. Page silent.
450: 21 cells of Jin's west-south edge pass to Chu in Cliopatria. Page silent on both pages.

403: Han is recognised as a marquisate. 'So, in 403 BCE, they divided the state's lands among themselves'; 'This same year, King Weilie of Zhou proclaimed Jin, Wei, Han, and Zhao as equals.' Cliopatria begins Han in 404; the real power had been theirs since the Zhi were destroyed in 453.
403: Wei is recognised as a marquisate (same sentence as Han).
403: Zhao is recognised as a marquisate (same sentence as Han).

region.text: the last Jin land around Jiang and Quwo

ledger.note: 369: the last Jin line ends. 'Modern historians... generally consider 369 BC the final year of Jin's existence'; the Bamboo Annals 'moved Duke Huan to Tunliu, and after that there were no more records'. Other pages: 376 deposition of Duke Jing 'marking the end of the Jin state' (Warring States period); 'In 349 BCE, the Han and Zhao states divided the remaining Jin territory between themselves' (Partition of Jin).

wars.name: Quwo-Jin conflict
wars.outcome: The Quwo branch conquered Jin in 678 and killed Marquis Min; Duke Wu ruled as Duke of Jin 678-677.
wars.note: The page dates 746 (Quwo as the capital of a fragment) and 678; no campaign is dated between.

wars.name: Jin-Qin wars
wars.outcome: Qin captured Duke Hui in 646 and restored him as a vassal; Jin defeated Qin in 627 and invaded in 625; no border moved.
wars.note: 'In 646 BC, Duke Hui was captured by Qin and restored as a vassal'; 'In 627 BC, Jin defeated Qin while it was attacking Zheng'; 'Jin invaded Qin in 625 BC and was driven back the following year'.

wars.name: Jin-Chu wars (Chengpu, Bi and Yanling)
wars.outcome: Jin and its allies defeated Chu at Chengpu (632) and Yanling (575); Chu defeated Jin in 598; Jin was recognised as hegemon; no border moved.
wars.note: 'Battle of Chengpu' (632, with Qin, Qi and Song); 'In 598 BC, Chu defeated Jin at the Battle of Mi' (the page's name and year); Yanling is the page's 'battle of Yingling' four years after 579.

wars.name: Battle of An
wars.outcome: Jin defeated Qi, which had invaded Lu and Wey.
wars.note: 'In 589 BC, Jin defeated Qi at the Battle of An, which had invaded Lu and Wey.'

wars.name: Wars among the Jin clans and the destruction of the Zhi

zones.text: Jinyang, where Zhao Xiangzi was besieged for two years

wars.outcome: Zhonghang, Fan and Handan attacked Zhao in 497; the Handan clan fell in 471 and Fan in 470; the Zhi besieged Jinyang from 455 and were annihilated by Zhao, Han and Wei in 453.
wars.note: 'Zhao Xiangzi retreated to the Jin city of Jinyang in 455 BCE, and the united forces laid siege to the city for two years'; 'In 453 BCE, the Zhao, Han, and Wei clans annihilated the Zhi clan.' The Jin page has 'about 450' and 'a long siege at Taiyuan'; Spring and Autumn period (not opened here) gives 497-453 for the whole civil war.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line exists for the whole life: the Jin frontier with the Rong, Di and neighbouring states is approximate, and the dukes' real domain after 453 is much smaller than the drawn shape.

notes: Wikidata Q6201794 is shared with 'former-jin' (Former Jin 922-925, the Later Tang precursor of Li Keyong and Li Cunxu): a different state; this dossier covers only the Cliopatria Name 'Jin' (-750..-405). Budget: 3 pages (2 allowed; the third, Eastern Zhou, dates the 635 grant), so the Jin shape changes at -550 and -450 and the Spring and Autumn annexations (Western Guo 687, Fan and Yuan 635, Gong 516 in that page's states table) are not dated or placed by a page opened here: they are confidence-1 events or notes. A gap-filler should open 'Spring and Autumn period' and the Jin annexation pages. Dates that disagree: end of Jin 369 (Jin page), 376 (Warring States period), 349 (Partition of Jin); the dukes' loss of real power 453 (Zhi destroyed) vs 403 (recognition) vs Cliopatria's shape drawn whole to 405. The Han, Wei and Zhao dossiers should take their land from 403 (page) rather than 404 (Cliopatria). Region names: 'Linfen' and 'Houma' are in the gazetteer; 'Quwo' is not and is given as coordinates (111.47 E, 35.64 N); gazetteer_names_needed: Quwo, Jiang, Xintian (Jin capitals).
